original_question: Let z_1, ..., z_k be points on a Hermitian manifold X, and let tau_1, ..., tau_k be positive numbers satisfying sum_j tau_j^n < integral_X omega^n. Construct an omega-plurisubharmonic function phi such that near each z_j one has phi(z) <= tau_j log ||z - z_j|| + O(1).
target_in_paper: Question 33 (Tosatti-Weinkove) in §4.3, “Prescribed singularities,” in the Hermitian-setting part of the paper. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s official formulation: it has the correct data (points z_1, ..., z_k and positive numbers τ_1, ..., τ_k), the correct numerical hypothesis Σ_j τ_j^n < ∫_X ω^n, and the correct target singularity condition φ(z) ≤ τ_j log ||z - z_j|| + O(1) near each z_j. In substance, it is a near-verbatim paraphrase of Question 33. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s ambient setting is a compact complex manifold X equipped with a Hermitian metric form ω; the section explicitly says X is compact and not necessarily Kähler. Your draft says only “Hermitian manifold,” so compactness and the role of ω as the Hermitian (1,1)-form are left implicit. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
The exponent n should be identified explicitly as the complex dimension n = dim_C X. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

For full stand-alone precision, one should define what “ω-plurisubharmonic” means in this section, namely φ ∈ PSH(X,ω) with ω + dd^cφ ≥ 0 in the sense of currents. The section introduces ω-plurisubharmonicity exactly through this inequality. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

The quantity ||z - z_j|| is only meaningful locally; to make the statement self-contained, one should specify that this norm is taken in local holomorphic coordinates centered at z_j, and that O(1) means a term locally bounded near z_j. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

Because the paper states this as an open problem, the stand-alone version should be phrased as an existence/construction question (“Does there exist” or “Can one construct”), rather than as an instruction presupposing a solution. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))

The nearby context in §4.3 explains the intended scope: the problem is about prescribed point singularities arising from Monge–Ampère equations whose right-hand sides concentrate at discrete points. This is not part of the formal question, but it clarifies the paper’s intent. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
refined_question: Let (X,ω) be a compact complex manifold of complex dimension n, equipped with a Hermitian metric form ω (so X is not assumed Kähler). Given points z_1, ..., z_k ∈ X and positive numbers τ_1, ..., τ_k satisfying Σ_{j=1}^k τ_j^n < ∫_X ω^n, can one construct a function φ ∈ PSH(X,ω) (equivalently, ω + dd^cφ ≥ 0 in the sense of currents) such that, in local holomorphic coordinates centered at each z_j, one has φ(z) ≤ τ_j log ||z - z_j|| + O(1) as z → z_j for every j = 1, ..., k? ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s Question 33, not at a broader neighboring problem. The match is direct: the inequality on the τ_j, the Hermitian setting, and the desired logarithmic upper bound near each prescribed point are exactly the ingredients of Question 33 in §4.3. The only additions needed to make it fully stand-alone come from the section-wide setup of §4 (compact complex manifold, Hermitian metric form ω, definition of ω-plurisubharmonicity) and from making the local-coordinate meaning of ||z-z_j|| explicit. The same paragraph also records the paper’s scope claim that Tosatti and Weinkove handled complex dimension 2 and, under extra assumptions, dimension 3, while the general case remains open. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~zeriahi/DGZ-arXiv2015.pdf))
